title: Add sandbox permission to allow native drag-and-drop between sandboxed/cross-origin iframes and parent

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: security-tracker
labels.description: Group bringing to attention of security, or tracked by the security Group but not needing response.

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

Native HTML5 Drag and Drop doesn't work reliably between a sandboxed iframe (without allow-same-origin) or a cross-origin iframe and its parent — even when both are controlled by the same app. This is a known, longstanding issue (e.g. Chromium Issue 251718). There's currently no sandbox value that re-enables just drag-and-drop data transfer across this boundary, without also granting full DOM/storage/cookie access via allow-same-origin.

### What solutions exist today?

Developers must reimplement drag-and-drop manually using pointerdown/pointermove/pointerup combined with postMessage, recreating a synthetic drag "ghost" element and manual hit-testing via elementFromPoint() on the parent. This works but loses native OS drag cursors, native file drag support, and accessibility affordances, and requires significant custom code for something the platform already provides natively within a single origin.

### How would you solve it?

Add a new sandbox token (e.g. allow-drag) that re-enables native dragstart/dragover/drop/dataTransfer behavior across the sandboxed/cross-origin boundary, without granting allow-same-origin's broader DOM, storage, and cookie access — the same pattern already used by allow-forms and allow-popups to re-enable one specific capability while keeping the rest of the sandbox intact.

### Anything else?

_No response_
